title: Chicken Fried Rice
description: Day-old rice, juicy chicken and a smoky wok toss. Better than takeout and ready in half an hour.

ingredients.name: Long-Grain White Rice
ingredients.note: cooked and chilled; day-old is best

steps.instruction: Dice the chicken and carrot into small, even pieces so everything cooks at the same speed.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Scramble the eggs until just set, then move them to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the chicken. Stir-fry until browned and cooked through (165°F / 74°C), 5–6 minutes.
Add the garlic, carrot and green onion whites; cook 1 minute. Add the peas.
Add the cold rice, breaking up clumps. Press it against the hot pan and toss every 30 seconds for 3–4 minutes so it toasts.
Add the soy sauce, sesame oil and eggs. Toss well, top with the green onion greens, and serve.

title: Beef and Broccoli
description: Tender, velvety beef and bright broccoli in a glossy garlic-ginger sauce.

steps.instruction: Toss the beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tsp cornstarch. Let it sit 15 minutes while you prep.
Cook the rice. Whisk the remaining soy sauce and cornstarch with the oyster sauce, brown sugar and 1/3 cup water.
Boil the broccoli for 1 minute, then drain. It finishes cooking in the sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Sear the beef in a single layer, in batches, about 1 minute per side. Remove.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, add the sauce and simmer until glossy, about 1 minute.
Return the beef and broccoli, toss to coat, and serve over rice.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
description: Sichuan classic with a tingle from Sichuan pepper, a little heat, tang from black vinegar and crunchy peanuts.

ingredients.name: Thai Chili
ingredients.note: halved; use fewer for less heat

steps.instruction: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp soy sauce and the cornstarch.
Stir together the remaining soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar and 2 tbsp water.
Heat the oil over medium. Fry the Sichuan peppercorns and chilies for 30 seconds until fragrant, not burnt.
Turn the heat to high, add the chicken and stir-fry until cooked through (165°F / 74°C), 5–6 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and green onions; cook 30 seconds. Pour in the sauce and toss until glossy.
Stir in the peanuts and serve right away with rice.

title: Mapo Tofu
description: Silky tofu in a bold, numbing, spicy pork sauce built on doubanjiang (chili bean paste).

ingredients.name: Tofu
ingredients.note: soft or medium, cut into 1-inch cubes

steps.instruction: Gently simmer the tofu cubes in salted water for 2 minutes to firm them up, then drain.
Heat the oil over medium-high. Brown the pork, breaking it up, 4–5 minutes.
Add the doubanjiang, garlic and ginger and cook until the oil turns red, about 1 minute.
Add the broth and soy sauce, slide in the tofu, and simmer 5 minutes without stirring hard.
Stir the cornstarch mix, drizzle it in and nudge gently until the sauce thickens.
Finish with ground Sichuan pepper and green onions. Serve with rice.

title: Pork and Cabbage Potstickers
description: Juicy pork dumplings with crisp, golden bottoms. Makes about 36; they freeze beautifully.

steps.instruction: Toss the cabbage with the salt, wait 10 minutes, then squeeze out as much water as you can.
Mix the pork, cabbage, green onions, ginger, garlic, soy sauce and sesame oil until sticky.
Put a heaping teaspoon of filling in each wrapper, wet the edge, fold and pleat to seal.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a nonstick skillet over medium. Add dumplings flat-side down and fry until golden, 2 minutes.
Add 1/3 cup water, cover, and steam until the water is gone and the filling reaches 160°F (71°C), about 6 minutes.
Uncover and crisp the bottoms another minute. Repeat with the rest and serve with black vinegar.

title: Egg Drop Soup
description: Silky ribbons of egg in seasoned broth: a ten-minute comfort soup.

steps.instruction: Bring the broth, soy sauce and ginger to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch mix and simmer until slightly thickened, 1 minute.
Stir the soup in one direction, then slowly drizzle in the eggs so they form ribbons.
Turn off the heat, add the sesame oil and green onions, and serve.

title: Scallion Pancakes
description: Flaky, chewy pan-fried flatbreads layered with green onions.

steps.instruction: Mix the flour with 3/4 cup just-boiled water, then knead until smooth, about 5 minutes. Rest covered 30 minutes.
Divide into 4. Roll each very thin, brush with sesame oil, sprinkle with salt and green onions.
Roll each up like a rope, coil it into a snail, and roll flat again to about 7 inches.
Pan-fry each in hot oil over medium until golden and crisp, 2–3 minutes per side.
Cut into wedges and serve with soy sauce mixed with rice vinegar.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
description: Crisp-skinned chicken in a sticky, from-scratch teriyaki glaze.

steps.instruction: Cook the rice. Whisk the soy sauce, mirin, honey, ginger and garlic.
Heat the oil over medium-high. Cook the chicken skin-side down without moving until crisp, 7–8 minutes. Flip.
Cook until 165°F (74°C) inside, about 5 more minutes. Pour off excess fat.
Add the sauce and the cornstarch mix; simmer, turning the chicken, until thick and glossy.
Rest 3 minutes, slice, and top with sesame seeds and green onions.

title: Miso-Glazed Salmon
description: Sweet, savory, caramelized miso glaze on flaky salmon, under the broiler in minutes.

steps.instruction: Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches from the heat. Line a sheet pan with foil.
Whisk the miso, mirin, honey and vinegar. Spread over the tops of the salmon.
Broil until the glaze is deeply browned in spots and the salmon flakes easily (145°F / 63°C), 7–10 minutes. Watch closely.
Top with sesame seeds and green onions.

title: Chicken Katsu
description: Panko-crusted cutlets fried golden, with a quick tangy katsu sauce and crunchy cabbage.

steps.instruction: Season the chicken with salt. Set up three plates: flour, eggs, panko.
Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then press firmly into panko.
Heat 1/2 inch of oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry the cutlets until deep golden and 165°F (74°C) inside, 3–4 minutes per side.
Drain on a rack for 3 minutes so the crust stays crisp.
Stir together ketchup, Worcestershire, soy sauce and sugar for the sauce.
Slice and serve with the cabbage and sauce.

title: Miso Soup with Tofu and Spinach
description: Simple, savory miso soup. The key: never let the miso boil.

steps.instruction: Simmer the broth and mushrooms for 5 minutes.
Add the tofu and spinach and heat through, 1 minute. Turn the heat to low.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of hot broth until smooth, then stir it back in. Don't boil it after this.
Top with green onions and serve.

title: Yaki Udon with Chicken
description: Thick, chewy udon stir-fried with chicken, cabbage and mushrooms in a savory sauce.

steps.instruction: Cook the udon per the package, drain and rinse briefly.
Heat the oil over high. Stir-fry the chicken until cooked through (165°F / 74°C), 4–5 minutes.
Add the cabbage, mushrooms and carrot; stir-fry until just tender, 3 minutes.
Add the noodles, soy sauce, mirin and oyster sauce. Toss until glossy and hot.
Add the green onions and sesame oil and serve.

title: Bibimbap
description: Rice topped with seasoned vegetables, savory beef, a fried egg and spicy-sweet gochujang sauce.

steps.instruction: Cook the rice. Stir the gochujang with 1 tbsp sesame oil, the honey and 1 tbsp water for the sauce.
Blanch the spinach 30 seconds and the bean sprouts 1 minute; squeeze dry and season each with a little sesame oil and soy sauce.
Sauté the carrot, zucchini and mushrooms separately in a little oil until just tender, salting lightly.
Brown the beef with the garlic and 2 tbsp soy sauce until cooked through (160°F / 71°C).
Fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Divide the rice into bowls, arrange everything on top, and finish with sesame seeds and the sauce. Mix before eating.

title: Beef Bulgogi
description: Thin-sliced beef in a sweet-savory pear marinade, seared until caramelized at the edges.

ingredients.name: Ribeye Steak
ingredients.note: very thinly sliced (freeze 30 minutes first to make slicing easy)

steps.instruction: Mix the soy sauce, pear, brown sugar, garlic, ginger and sesame oil. Add the beef and onion; marinate 30 minutes to 4 hours in the fridge.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over high. Cook the beef in batches in a single layer until browned and caramelized, 2–3 minutes.
Top with green onions and sesame seeds. Serve with rice and lettuce leaves for wrapping.

title: Kimchi Fried Rice
description: Tangy, spicy, buttery fried rice crowned with a runny egg. A great use for leftover rice.

ingredients.name: Kimchi
ingredients.note: chopped, plus 2 tbsp of its juice

steps.instruction: Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium until crisp.
Add the kimchi and cook 2–3 minutes until it starts to caramelize.
Add the rice, gochujang and kimchi juice. Press and toss over high heat until hot and a little crispy.
Stir in the butter and sesame oil. Fry the eggs in another pan until the whites are set.
Serve the rice topped with the eggs and green onions.

title: Spicy Gochujang Pork (Jeyuk Bokkeum)
description: Fiery, sweet stir-fried pork. Wrap it in lettuce with rice.

steps.instruction: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, honey, garlic, ginger and sesame oil. Toss with the pork and marinate 20 minutes.
Heat the oil over high. Stir-fry the pork and onion until the pork is cooked through (145°F / 63°C) and the edges char, 6–8 minutes.
Add the green onions, toss 30 seconds, and serve with lettuce and rice.

title: Shrimp Pad Thai
description: Sweet, sour, salty rice noodles with shrimp, egg, bean sprouts and peanuts.

steps.instruction: Soak the noodles in hot tap water until pliable but still firm, about 15 minutes. Drain.
Stir together fish sauce, brown sugar, vinegar, lime juice and sriracha.
Heat the oil over high. Stir-fry the shrimp and garlic until the shrimp turn pink and opaque, 2 minutes.
Push everything aside, scramble the eggs in the empty space, then add the noodles and sauce. Toss until the noodles soften and absorb the sauce.
Add the bean sprouts and green onions, toss 30 seconds, and serve with peanuts and lime wedges.

title: Thai Green Curry with Chicken
description: Fragrant coconut curry with tender chicken, vegetables and Thai basil.

steps.instruction: Cook the rice.
Heat the oil over medium. Fry the curry paste with a few spoonfuls of the thick coconut cream until fragrant, 1–2 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir to coat, then the rest of the coconut milk, broth, lime leaves, fish sauce and sugar.
Simmer until the chicken is cooked through (165°F / 74°C), 8–10 minutes. Add the zucchini and pepper for the last 4 minutes.
Stir in the basil and serve over rice.

title: Thai Basil Chicken (Pad Kra Pao)
description: A Bangkok street-food favorite: garlicky, spicy ground chicken with holy or Thai basil and a crispy fried egg.

steps.instruction: Cook the rice. Mix the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar and 2 tbsp water.
Fry the eggs in 2 tbsp hot oil until the edges are crispy. Set aside.
In the remaining oil, cook the garlic, shallots and chilies over high heat for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until cooked through (165°F / 74°C), 4–5 minutes. Add the sauce.
Turn off the heat and fold in the basil until wilted. Serve over rice with a fried egg.

title: Tom Kha Gai (Coconut Chicken Soup)
description: Creamy, tangy coconut soup scented with lemongrass and lime leaf. Made without chilies so it fits AIP.

steps.instruction: Simmer the coconut milk, broth, lemongrass, ginger and lime leaves for 10 minutes to infuse.
Add the chicken and mushrooms and gently poach until the chicken is cooked through (165°F / 74°C), 5–7 minutes.
Turn off the heat and stir in the fish sauce and lime juice. Taste: it should be tangy, salty and rich.
Remove the lemongrass and ginger if you like, and top with cilantro.

title: Fresh Shrimp Spring Rolls
description: Translucent rice-paper rolls packed with shrimp, herbs and noodles, with a peanut-hoisin dip.

steps.instruction: Boil the shrimp until pink and opaque, about 2 minutes. Cool and halve lengthwise.
Cook the noodles per the package, rinse in cold water and drain.
Dip one rice paper in warm water for 5 seconds and lay it flat. It softens as you work.
Layer shrimp (pink side down), lettuce, noodles, vegetables and herbs. Fold in the sides and roll tightly.
For the dip, whisk the peanut butter, hoisin, vinegar and 2–3 tbsp warm water until smooth.

title: Lemongrass Pork Noodle Bowls (Bun Thit Nuong)
description: Caramelized lemongrass pork over cool noodles, crisp vegetables, herbs and a bright dressing.

steps.instruction: Mix the lemongrass, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, half the garlic, the shallots and oil. Marinate the pork 30 minutes.
Toss the carrot with the vinegar and a pinch of sugar; let sit while you cook.
Grill or broil the pork until caramelized and cooked through (145°F / 63°C), 3–4 minutes per side.
Cook the noodles, rinse in cold water and drain.
For the dressing, stir the lime juice, remaining fish sauce and sugar, the rest of the garlic, the chili and 1/4 cup water.
Build bowls: lettuce, noodles, vegetables, herbs, pork, peanuts. Spoon over the dressing.

title: Chicken Pho
description: Aromatic broth with charred onion, ginger and star anise, poured over rice noodles and tender chicken.

steps.instruction: Broil the onion and ginger cut-side up until charred, about 10 minutes.
Toast the star anise in a dry pot for 1 minute, then add the broth, onion, ginger, cinnamon, fish sauce and sugar. Simmer 30 minutes.
Add the chicken and poach gently until 165°F (74°C), 15–20 minutes. Remove, rest, and slice.
Strain the broth. Cook the noodles per the package.
Divide the noodles and chicken into bowls, ladle over the hot broth, and serve with sprouts, herbs, lime, hoisin and sriracha.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Yogurt-marinated chicken charred under the broiler, then simmered in a creamy spiced tomato sauce.

steps.instruction: Mix the yogurt, 1 tbsp garam masala, half the garlic and ginger, and the salt. Coat the chicken and marinate at least 30 minutes.
Broil the chicken on a foil-lined pan until charred in spots, about 10 minutes. It finishes in the sauce.
Melt the butter over medium. Cook the onion until golden, 8 minutes, then the rest of the garlic and ginger and all the spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes. Stir in the cream and chicken and simmer until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Top with cilantro and serve with rice.

title: Chana Masala
description: Hearty spiced chickpeas in a tangy tomato-onion sauce. Pantry-friendly and better the next day.

steps.instruction: Heat the oil over medium and cook the onion until deep golden, 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and all the spices; stir 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, salt and 1/2 cup water. Simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken.
Stir in the lemon juice, top with cilantro, and serve with rice.

title: Coconut Red Lentil Dal
description: Creamy, golden lentils simmered with coconut milk and warm spices, finished with spinach and lemon.

steps.instruction: Cook the onion in the oil over medium until soft, 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, coconut milk, broth and salt. Simmer, stirring now and then, until the lentils break down, 18–20 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then the lemon juice. Serve with rice or naan.

title: Chicken Adobo
description: The Philippines' beloved braise: chicken in soy, vinegar, garlic and bay leaf, reduced to a glossy sauce.

steps.instruction: Brown the chicken skin-side down in the oil over medium-high until golden, 6–8 minutes.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the soy sauce, vinegar, 1/2 cup water, bay leaves, peppercorns and sugar. Don't stir for the first few minutes so the vinegar mellows.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is very tender (at least 165°F / 74°C), 30–35 minutes.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce reduces and turns glossy, 5–10 minutes.
Top with green onions and serve with rice.

title: AIP Chicken Adobo
description: All the tang of classic adobo, made AIP-friendly with coconut aminos and apple cider vinegar and no peppercorns.

steps.instruction: Season the chicken with salt and brown it skin-side down in the oil until golden, 6–8 minutes.
Add the garlic, coconut aminos, vinegar, 1/3 cup water and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer gently until very tender (at least 165°F / 74°C), 30–35 minutes.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until glossy, 5–10 minutes. Coconut aminos is sweeter than soy, so it thickens quickly.
Top with green onions. Serve with cauliflower rice or roasted sweet potatoes to keep it AIP.

title: AIP Ginger-Garlic Shrimp Stir-Fry
description: A fast, savory stir-fry with a coconut aminos sauce. No soy, seeds or nightshades.

steps.instruction: Heat 1 tbsp oil over high. Stir-fry the shrimp until pink and opaque, 2 minutes. Remove.
Add the rest of the oil, then the broccoli, carrot and mushrooms with 2 tbsp water; cook until crisp-tender, 3–4 minutes.
Add the bok choy, garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.
Return the shrimp, add the coconut aminos and arrowroot mix, and toss until glossy.
Season with salt, top with green onions and serve with lime.

title: AIP Cauliflower Fried Rice
description: Everything you love about fried rice, made with cauliflower: no rice, eggs, soy or seed oils.

ingredients.name: Cauliflower
ingredients.note: riced (pulsed in a food processor) or 4 cups pre-riced

steps.instruction: Dice the vegetables small so they cook as fast as the cauliflower.
Brown the pork in 1 tbsp oil over medium-high until cooked through (160°F / 71°C). Remove.
Add the remaining oil and the carrot, garlic and ginger; stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add the cauliflower and spread it out. Let it sit 2 minutes to brown, then toss. Cook until tender but not mushy, 5–6 minutes total.
Add the bok choy, pork, coconut aminos and fish sauce; toss 1–2 minutes. Season and top with green onions.

title: AIP Chicken Teriyaki
description: A sticky, glossy teriyaki-style glaze made with coconut aminos and honey, thickened with arrowroot.

steps.instruction: Season the chicken with salt and sear in the oil over medium-high until golden, 5–6 minutes per side, and 165°F (74°C) inside.
Steam the broccoli until bright and tender, 4–5 minutes.
Whisk the coconut aminos, honey, ginger and garlic. Pour into the pan with the chicken.
Simmer, turning the chicken, until reduced by half. Stir in the arrowroot mix until glossy.
Slice, spoon over the sauce, and serve with the broccoli and green onions.

title: AIP Chicken Lettuce Wraps
description: Savory, crunchy ground chicken with mushrooms and ginger, spooned into crisp lettuce cups.

steps.instruction: Finely chop the mushrooms and carrot so the filling holds together in the lettuce.
Heat the oil over medium-high. Cook the chicken, breaking it up, until cooked through (165°F / 74°C), 5–6 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, carrot, garlic and ginger; cook until the mushrooms soften, 3 minutes.
Stir in the coconut aminos, vinegar and most of the green onions. Season with salt.
Spoon into lettuce leaves and top with cilantro, the rest of the green onions and a squeeze of lime.

title: AIP Turmeric Coconut Chicken Curry
description: Golden, gently spiced coconut curry with sweet potato and spinach, warm from ginger and turmeric rather than chili.

steps.instruction: Cook the onion in the coconut oil over medium until soft, 6 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric and cinnamon for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and stir to coat.
Add the coconut milk, broth, sweet potato and salt. Simmer until the sweet potato is tender and the chicken is 165°F (74°C), about 20 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and lime juice. Top with cilantro and serve with cauliflower rice.

title: AIP Thai-Style Basil Beef
description: The garlicky, basil-packed flavor of pad kra pao, without chilies, soy or oyster sauce.

steps.instruction: Sauté the riced cauliflower in a little oil until tender, 5 minutes. Set aside.
Heat the oil over high and cook the garlic and shallots for 30 seconds.
Add the beef and stir-fry until browned and cooked through (160°F / 71°C), 5 minutes.
Add the coconut aminos and fish sauce, then fold in the basil until wilted.
Serve over the cauliflower rice with lime.

title: AIP Steamed Cod with Ginger and Scallion
description: Delicate steamed fish finished with sizzling oil poured over fresh ginger and green onions.

steps.instruction: Season the fish with salt and place on a heatproof plate. Scatter half the ginger on top.
Steam over simmering water, covered, until the fish flakes easily (145°F / 63°C), 8–10 minutes.
Pour off the liquid on the plate. Top with the rest of the ginger and the green onions, and drizzle with coconut aminos.
Heat the oil until shimmering and carefully pour it over the ginger and green onions so they sizzle. Top with cilantro.

title: AIP Vietnamese-Style Lemongrass Chicken
description: Caramelized lemongrass-honey chicken with cucumber and fresh herbs.

steps.instruction: Mix the lemongrass, fish sauce, honey, garlic, shallots and 1 tbsp oil. Marinate the chicken at least 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear over medium-high until charred and 165°F (74°C) inside, 5–6 minutes per side.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Serve with cucumber, herbs and lime.

title: AIP Herb-Roasted Chicken and Sweet Potatoes
description: One pan, crispy chicken thighs and caramelized sweet potatoes with rosemary, thyme and lemon.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the sweet potatoes, onion and garlic with 2 tbsp oil, half the herbs and half the salt on a sheet pan.
Rub the chicken with the rest of the oil, herbs and salt. Nestle it skin-side up among the vegetables, with the lemon halves.
Roast until the skin is crisp and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C), 35–40 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes and squeeze the roasted lemon over everything.

title: AIP Mashed Sweet Potatoes
description: Silky mashed sweet potatoes made creamy with coconut milk, with a hint of cinnamon. Dairy-free and AIP.

steps.instruction: Cover the sweet potatoes with cold salted water, bring to a boil, and cook until very tender, 15–18 minutes.
Drain well and let them steam-dry in the pot for 2 minutes.
Mash with the coconut oil, then add the warm coconut milk until creamy. Season with salt and cinnamon.

title: AIP Balsamic Garlic Mushrooms
description: Deeply browned mushrooms glazed with balsamic and garlic. A great side for anything.

steps.instruction: Heat the oil over medium-high. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and leave them alone until browned, 4–5 minutes. Stir and brown again.
Add the garlic and thyme for 30 seconds.
Add the balsamic and stir until it coats the mushrooms and the pan is nearly dry.
Season with salt and serve.

title: AIP Lemon-Dill Salmon with Asparagus
description: Simple sheet-pan salmon and asparagus with lemon, garlic and fresh dill.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss the asparagus with 1 tbsp oil and some salt on a sheet pan. Push to the sides.
Place the salmon in the center. Mix the rest of the oil with the garlic, lemon zest, dill and salt; spread over the fish. Top with lemon slices.
Roast until the salmon flakes easily (145°F / 63°C), 12–15 minutes.

title: AIP Hearty Beef Stew
description: Fall-apart beef with carrots, parsnips and herbs in a rich broth. No potatoes or tomatoes.

ingredients.name: Beef Broth
ingredients.note: no added sugar or seed spices

steps.instruction: Season the beef with salt. Brown it in batches in the oil over medium-high, 3–4 minutes per batch. Don't crowd the pot.
Cook the onion in the drippings until soft, 5 minutes. Add the garlic, then the balsamic, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the beef, add the broth, bay leaves and thyme. Cover and simmer gently 1.5 hours.
Add the carrots, parsnips and celery and simmer until the beef is fork-tender, 45 minutes more.
Stir in the arrowroot mix and simmer 2 minutes to thicken. Remove the bay leaves and season.

title: AIP Carnitas Lettuce Tacos
description: Citrus-braised pork, shredded and broiled until crispy, in lettuce cups with avocado. No cumin or chili.

steps.instruction: Season the pork with salt and oregano.
Brown the pork in the oil over medium-high, in batches.
Add the citrus juice, garlic, bay leaves and 1/2 cup water. Cover and cook low (or at 325°F / 165°C in the oven) until falling apart, about 2.5 hours.
Shred with two forks and spread on a sheet pan with a few spoonfuls of the cooking liquid.
Broil until the edges crisp, 4–6 minutes.
Serve in lettuce with avocado, cilantro, onion and lime.

title: AIP Sweet Potato Sausage Hash
description: Homemade sage breakfast sausage with crispy sweet potatoes and kale. Egg-free and AIP.

steps.instruction: Mix the pork, sage, garlic powder, ginger and 1 tsp salt. That's your sausage.
Brown the sausage in a large skillet over medium-high until cooked through (160°F / 71°C). Remove.
Add the oil, sweet potatoes, onion and the rest of the salt. Cover and cook 5 minutes to soften.
Uncover and cook, stirring only every few minutes, until crispy and tender, 10 minutes.
Add the kale and sausage and cook until the kale wilts.

title: AIP Rosemary Roasted Root Vegetables
description: Sweet, caramelized carrots, parsnips and beets with rosemary.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss everything on a sheet pan in a single layer. Use two pans if crowded, so they roast instead of steam.
Roast, turning once, until caramelized and tender, 30–35 minutes.

title: AIP Chicken and Vegetable Soup
description: Healing, simple chicken soup with bone broth, root vegetables and greens. No noodles needed.

steps.instruction: Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the oil until softened, 6–8 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the broth, chicken, thyme, bay leaves and salt.
Simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through (165°F / 74°C), 20–25 minutes.
Shred the chicken and return it. Add the kale and simmer 5 minutes. Finish with parsley.

title: AIP Guacamole
description: Bright, chunky guacamole without tomato or chili, so it stays AIP.

steps.instruction: Finely dice the onion; it tames the bite.
Mash the avocados with the lime juice, leaving some chunks.
Fold in the onion, cilantro, garlic and salt. Taste and adjust.

title: AIP Lemon-Garlic Shrimp with Zucchini
description: Fast, bright shrimp and tender zucchini in lemon-garlic olive oil.

steps.instruction: Sauté the zucchini in 1 tbsp oil over medium-high until golden at the edges, 4 minutes. Remove.
Add the rest of the oil and the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook until pink and opaque, about 1–2 minutes per side.
Return the zucchini, add the lemon zest and juice, salt and parsley, and toss.

title: Spaghetti Bolognese
description: A slow-simmered meat sauce with wine, milk and tomato. Worth the wait.

steps.instruction: Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery.
Cook them in the oil over medium until soft and sweet, 10 minutes.
Add the beef and garlic; cook until no longer pink. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the wine and scrape up the browned bits, then simmer until mostly gone.
Add the milk and simmer until absorbed, then the tomatoes, bay leaves and salt.
Simmer very gently, partly covered, for 1 to 1.5 hours, stirring now and then.
Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water until al dente, toss with the sauce and serve with Parmesan.

title: Classic Beef and Bean Chili
description: Thick, smoky, crowd-pleasing chili with the toppings bar of your choice.

steps.instruction: Brown the beef in a large pot over medium-high. Pour off most of the fat.
Add the onion and pepper and cook until soft, 6 minutes. Add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, tomato sauce, beans, broth and salt. Simmer uncovered, stirring now and then, until thick, 45–60 minutes.
Serve with cheddar and sour cream.

title: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes
description: Tall, tender pancakes. The trick is a lumpy batter.

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: melted, plus more for the pan

steps.instruction: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Whisk the buttermilk, eggs and melted butter in another bowl.
Fold the wet into the dry just until no dry flour remains. Lumps are good; overmixing makes tough pancakes.
Rest the batter 5 minutes while a griddle heats over medium.
Butter the griddle and pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Flip when bubbles pop on top, 2–3 minutes, then cook 1–2 minutes more.
Serve with maple syrup.

title: Garlic Butter Steak Bites
description: Seared sirloin cubes basted in garlic-thyme butter. Weeknight steakhouse.

steps.instruction: Season the steak well with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet until smoking. Sear the steak in a single layer, in batches, 1–2 minutes per side.
Lower the heat, add the butter, garlic and thyme, return all the steak and spoon the foaming butter over it for 1 minute (medium-rare is 130–135°F / 54–57°C).
Top with parsley and serve right away.

title: Baked Mac and Cheese
description: Creamy, two-cheese baked macaroni with a crunchy panko top.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Boil the macaroni 2 minutes less than the package says; it finishes in the oven. Drain.
Melt 4 tbsp butter, whisk in the flour, and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the warm milk and simmer until thickened, 4–5 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the cheeses, mustard and salt until smooth. Fold in the pasta.
Pour into a baking dish. Toss the panko with the remaining butter, melted, and sprinkle on top.
Bake until bubbling and golden, 20–25 minutes.

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs gently poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, with feta and herbs. Great with bread.

steps.instruction: Cook the onion and pepper in the oil over medium until soft, 8 minutes. Add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer until thickened, 10 minutes.
Make 6 wells with a spoon and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook on low until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, 5–8 minutes.
Top with feta and cilantro.

title: Crispy Black Bean Tacos
description: Smoky, crispy black bean tacos with avocado and a squeeze of lime.

steps.instruction: Warm the beans with 1 tbsp oil, the garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt and 2 tbsp water, mashing about half.
Fill each tortilla with a spoonful of beans and fold in half.
Pan-fry the tacos in the remaining oil over medium until crisp, 2–3 minutes per side.
Open gently and add avocado, onion, cilantro and feta. Serve with lime.

title: Honey-Mustard Baked Salmon
description: A sweet-tangy glaze that turns salmon into a 20-minute dinner.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Season the salmon with salt and pepper and place on a lined sheet pan.
Whisk the mustard, honey, oil and garlic; brush over the salmon.
Bake until the salmon flakes easily (145°F / 63°C), 12–15 minutes.
Serve with lemon.

title: Smash Burgers
description: Thin, lacy-edged burgers with melty cheese. A screaming-hot pan is the secret.

steps.instruction: Heat a cast-iron skillet or griddle over high for 5 minutes.
Put 2 balls in the pan and immediately smash them very thin with a sturdy spatula. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook until the edges are deeply browned and crisp, about 2 minutes. Scrape up, flip, and top each with cheese.
Cook 1 minute more, until 160°F (71°C). Stack two patties per bun.
Top with onion, pickles, ketchup and mustard. Repeat.

title: Brown Butter Banana Bread
description: Moist, deeply flavored banana bread. The riper the bananas, the better.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Melt the butter over medium and cook, swirling, until it smells nutty and turns golden brown, 4–5 minutes. Cool slightly.
Mash the bananas, then whisk in the brown butter, sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Fold in the flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon just until combined.
Bake until a toothpick in the center comes out clean, 55–65 minutes.
Cool 15 minutes in the pan, then on a rack.

title: Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Crisp edges, chewy centers, lots of chocolate. Makes about 24.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the butter and both sugars until light and fluffy, 3 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour, baking soda and salt, then the chocolate chips.
Scoop 2-tablespoon balls 2 inches apart.
Bake until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle, 10–12 minutes. Cool 5 minutes on the sheet.
